Third St. City Council Agenda August 17, 2026 Page 1 of 3 The Moscow Mayor, City Council and Staff welcome you to tonight’s meeting. This meeting is open to the public. We appreciate and encourage public participation. For regular agenda items, an opportunity for public comment is sometimes provided after the staff report. However, the formality of procedures varies with the purpose and subject of the agenda item; therefore, the Mayor may exercise discretion in deciding when to allow public comment during the course of the proceedings and limitations may be placed on the time allowed for comments. Citizens wishing to comment on business that is not on the agenda will be provided the opportunity to do so during the public comment item on the agenda. If you plan to address the Council, you will find a list of “Tips for Addressing the Council” in the door pocket outside the City Council Chambers. Please note that Moscow City Council meetings are televised, videotaped and/or recorded. Links to view the City Council meeting live can be found on the City website and the City’s YouTube channel. Thank you for your interest in City government. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE CONSENT AGENDA 1. All Consent Items (ACTION ITEM) A. Approval of Moscow City Council August 3, 2026 Minutes - Laurie M. Hopkins B. Approval of Payment of Claims - Sarah Decker C. Disbursement Report July 2026 - Sarah Decker Staff presented the July 2026 Accounts Payable Report to the Public Works / Finance Committee on August 10th, 2026. The Committee received the report and recommended approval of the disbursement report. ACTION: Accept the Disbursements Report for the month of July 2026. D. Cooperative Agreement for Future Traffic Signal Installation - Nichoel Baird Spencer In 2025, the City of Moscow entered into a development agreement with the developers of the SOMO development in south Moscow, which included the collection of the developers' proportionate share fee toward the cost of the future traffic signal installation at the intersection of Somo Drive/Reisenauer Road and U.S. Highway 95. The Idaho Transportation Department (ITD) has requested that the City enter into an agreement to convey the collected fees to ITD at the time the signal is installed. Staff has prepared an agreement for the Council's review and approval. This was reviewed by the Public Works/Finance Committee on August 10, 2026, and recommended for approval. ACTION: Approve the Cooperative Agreement with Idaho Transportation Department.

South HWY 95 Pathway Extension - Bid Results & Contract Award - Luke Hajda The South HWY 95 Pathway Extension's Project scope is to connect an existing shared-use path on Reisenauer Rd (adjacent to the Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories property) north to an existing sidewalk section on US-95. The project is to construct a ten-foot wide shared- use path from Reisenauer Rd to the existing sidewalk. The City sent out a semi-formal request for bids on July 17, 2026, and the Engineer's Estimate for construction was $145,449.00. Bids were opened July 23, 2026. The City received one bid in the amount of $141,263.20 from Motley-Motley, Inc. of Pullman, WA. A bid tabulation is included in the packet. This was reviewed by the Public Works / Finance Committee on August 10, 2026, and recommended for approval. ACTION: Accept the bid from Motely-Motley. Inc, award the contract in the amount of $141,263.20 and authorize staff approval of construction change orders in an amount not to exceed 10% of the contract amount. REGULAR AGENDA 2. Public Comment (limit 15 minutes) 3. PUBLIC HEARING: City of Moscow FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance (ACTION ITEM) - Bill Belknap / Sarah Decker Staff will present the proposed City of Moscow FY2027 budget in the amount of $149,942,154, which was considered by the City Council at a workshop held on July 8, 2026. The proposed budget includes the statutorily allowed 3% inflationary increase, the remaining $15,141 foregone tax, as well as 90% of new construction at $189,064. According to the Latah County Assessor’s office, the assessed taxable valuation within the City increased by 4.7% this year, which resulted in a reduction of the City’s levy rate from $3.57 to $3.51 per $1,000 in taxable valuation. Included for City Council consideration are the FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance, the foregone Resolution, and the L-2 property tax certification in the aggregate amount of $9,445,604. PROPOSED ACTIONS: Conduct the public hearing upon the FY2027 City of Moscow Annual Appropriation Ordinance, and upon consideration of testimony presented: 1. Approve the foregone tax recovery Resolution, or take other action as deemed appropriate; and 2. Approve the appropriation ordinance under suspension of the rules requiring three complete and separate readings and that it be read by title and published by summary; or consider the Ordinance on first reading and that it be read by title; or reject the Ordinance; or take other action deemed appropriate; and 3. Authorize the Mayor’s execution of the L-2 property tax certification in the aggregate amount of $9,445,604; or take such other action deemed appropriate. 4. PUBLIC HEARING: Proposed FY2027 Fee Resolution (ACTION ITEM) - Bill Belknap Any new fees or increases to existing fees by more than 5% require a public hearing pursuant to Idaho Code 63-1311A. Additionally, as required by Idaho Code 63-1311, the City's fees collected shall be reasonably related to the actual cost of the service provided. Staff will discuss proposed fee increases for the FY2027 budget year, which support the FY2027 budget proposal. The fee increases are due to the additional costs associated with the delivery of services, including administration, operations, and maintenance. Fees proposed to be adjusted include the following: arts programs, land use and development fees, construction permit fees and fees related to inspections; increases to sanitation rates, water permit and service rates; sewer permit and service rates; street closure and traffic control; and stormwater rates. Other miscellaneous fee changes are

CONSENT AGENDA 1. All Consent Items (ACTION ITEM) A. Approval of Moscow City Council July 20, 2026 Minutes - Laurie M. Hopkins B. Approval of Payment of Claims - Sarah Decker C. Camp Moscowanna Alcohol Use Request in Entertainment District - Amanda Argona The Moscow Chamber of Commerce + Visitor Center is hosting Camp Moscowanna on Saturday, August 15th, from 4 pm to 8 pm on Main Street between 3rd and 6th Streets. This summer camp- themed event is designed to evoke the nostalgia of family-friendly gatherings and will feature retail vendors offering a variety of activities with highlights including bean bag toss, knot tying, s'more making, and general crafting. Eight food vendors are expected, and no more than four beer/wine vendors will be present. The event has been reviewed and approved by staff on 29, 2026. Following standard operating procedures for events with alcohol that are within the Entertainment District boundaries, Camp Moscowanna is requesting a temporary suspension of the open container law by resolution. Per Moscow City Code, Section 10-1-12, a draft resolution has been prepared for the Council's consideration. ACTION: Approve the resolution allowing for the temporary suspension of the open container law within the event footprint of Camp Moscowanna for the duration of the event. Holmes moved and Davis seconded to approve the consent agenda as presented. Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Unanimous. Nays: None. Abstentions: None. Motion carried. REGULAR AGENDA 2. Mayors Appointments (ACTION ITEM) None offered. DRAFT Page 4

City Council Minutes August 3, 2026 Page 2 of 4 3. Public Comment (limit 15 minutes) None offered. 4. Citizen Commission Report– Sustainable Environment Commission - Kelli Cooper / Steve McGeehan Cooper introduced McGeehan, chair of the commission. The Commission reviewed and supported updates to the water conservation plan; discussed and supported the Energy Efficiency Electrification (EEE) Fair; and requested and reviewed the Mayor's Earth Day Awards. The EEE Fair included contractors, energy experts, tax and rebate information, presentations, and panel discussions. The Commission has been discussing community solar feasibility with the intention of drafting a framework of what a community solar project could look like for Moscow. The second annual Electric Transportation Fair will take place September 11. Mayor Lewis said there is a poster circulating that mentions a community solar array on the new City shop but the shop was never a suggested location. The City has received a lot of emails regarding this community solar. While it will come down to what the utility can make sense of, she is excited people are passionate and looking into it. The Climate Action Working Group is now working on the solar project. Blankenship thanked the Commission for helping make the EEE Fair a success. Sumner is excited to hear about the alternate forms of energy. 5. Police Department Donation Account Creation Resolution (ACTION ITEM) - Bill Belknap Resident Joyce Presby, who recently passed away, bequeathed a portion of her estate to several local organizations, including the Moscow Police Department. In accordance with her last will and testament and court-approved estate settlement distribution, the City received $24,818.35 from the estate. Staff is requesting to establish a restricted fund balance account for this gift and any other future donations that the Department may receive, for the future use of the Moscow Police Department, as approved by the Moscow City Council. In accordance with the City’s Financial Policies, the Council must authorize the creation of restricted fund balances and establish the purpose, intent, and use of the restricted funds. Staff has prepared a resolution authorizing the creation of a Moscow Police Department Donation Account as a restricted fund balance to be used in support of the Police Department as included within the City of Moscow annual budget and approved by the City Council. PROPOSED ACTIONS: Approve the proposed Resolution authorizing the creation of the Moscow Police Department Donation Account restricted fund balance; or take other action deemed appropriate. Belknap introduced the item as written above. It is not uncommon for the police department to receive contributions but are usually relatively small. There are no restrictions or stipulations on the use. Chief Dahlinger would like to hold the money for special training and special equipment, things outside the normal budgetary expenditures for the department. McCetich and Davis commented it is a very generous one time donation from a longtime community member. Sumner asked about a long-term fund that could build on earned interest. Belknap responded that usual contributions are usually less than a couple thousand per year so would take a considerable amount of time to establish a fund for a return on interest earnings. Holmes moved to approve the proposed Resolution authorizing the creation of the Moscow Police Department Donation Account restricted fund balance. Kelly seconded. Roll Call Vote: Ayes: Unanimous. Nays: None. Abstentions: None. Motion carried. DRAFT Page 5

City Council Minutes August 3, 2026 Page 3 of 4 6. East City Park Stage Update Report - David Schott Schott provided illustrations of the new stage including the floor plan. The improvements around the stage have been refined since the 30% design. Improvements include the pathway which swings on the south side around the stage. The stage itself will have a new concreate pathway ring circling the stage with a grassy area in front of the stage. An area for loading and off-loading is designed as a hammer head so vehicles can turn around easily. The construction is out to bid with a bid opening scheduled for August 25 and the bids coming before council on September 21. Completion is anticipated by April 6 depending on the weather. The art installation is scheduled for May of 2027. The horseshoe pits will be demolished but a new pit will be installed on the west side of the park. The Ghormley pits will be revamped to make them regulation and tournament suitable. Blankenship liked the ring path around the stage and asked about plaza alternatives. Schott said both concrete and grass plaza’s have been requested. He feels this design is a solution to capture a vast majority of users. The dancer's plaza is a bid alternate. One tree at the north corner of the stage will need to be removed. Kelly had concerns regarding management and movement of people in regards to the bathrooms during events. Davis felt the stage is a good and positive thing for the community and feedback has been given through different venues. The concrete ring will be good for circulation and will enhance the space moving forward. Mayor Lewis was happy there are conversations about new grass being ready for the recurring spring events. McCetich asked for clarity on the concrete circle. Belknap explained the circle is a narrower concrete path creating a sense of place for the stage. The path south of the stage which goes southwest to northeast is for circulation through the park. The concrete circle provides a center aisle walkway during events to get people to concessions and/or bathroom and back to their seat. Holmes commented the concrete path is at the bottom of the sledding hill. He hopes the removal of the existing stage is done after the new stage is complete. Schott believes the demolition of the current stage would happen at the front end of the project so that the concrete ring can be installed and grass can be planted. The new construction won't start until after the summer events are concluded. Mayor Lewis stated she is having conversations with staff about incorporating pieces of the current stage. Blankenship said the MAC talked about that when he was liaison so happy to hear that. REPORTS City Council HPC - Kelly said they are talking about the historic district and how to present and share it. P&Z - McCetich said there was a public hearing on a development on the north side of Orchard. Mayor Mayor Lewis said she will be attending an aviation conference in Missoula. DRAFT Page 6

RECITALS WHEREAS, STATE has the authority under Idaho Code § 40-317 to enter into cooperative agreements with local governments for the construction and maintenance of transportation facilities; and WHEREAS, CITY is authorized under Idaho Code §§67-6503, 67-6511A, 67-6513, 67-6518, and Moscow City Code Title 5, Chapter 1, to enter into agreements for public improvements to mitigate the effects of subdivision development; and. Geotextile shall be Type II, nonwoven or woven, as set forth in Section 718.07 – Subgrade Separation Geotextile Property Requirements of the latest edition of the Idaho Transportation Department’s Standard Specifications for Highway Construction. The area to be covered shall be graded to a smooth uniform condition free of obstacles, depressions, and debris. The geotextile shall be spread immediately ahead of the covering operation. SOUTH HWY 95 PATHWAY EXTENSION - 2026 PAGE 107 OF 111 geotextile shall be placed loosely and without wrinkles so that placement of the overlying material will not tear the geotextile. The geotextile shall be lapped or sewn, as specified, at the ends and sides of adjoining sheets. The cover material shall be placed on the geotextile in such a manner that a minimum of six inches of material will be between the vehicle of equipment tires or tracks and the geotextile at all times. Where geotextiles will be placed over soft ground, construction vehicles shall be limited in size and weight such that rutting in the initial lift above the geotextile is not greater than three inches deep, to prevent overstressing the geotextile. Turning of vehicles on the first lift above the geotextile will not be permitted. End-dumping the cover material directly on the geotextile will not be permitted. Compaction of the first lift above the geotextile over soft ground shall be limited to routing of placing and spreading equipment only. No sheep foot type equipment will be allowed on the first lift. Subsequent lifts will be closely observed during compaction. If any foundation failures occur during compaction operations, lightweight compaction equipment shall be used. Pegs, pins or the manufacturer’s recommended method shall be used as needed to hold the geotextile in place until the specified cover material is placed. Under no circumstances shall cover material be dropped on unprotected geotextile from a height greater than three feet above the surface of the geotextile. The geotextile shall be covered with the specified cover material as soon as possible. Geotextiles which have not been ultraviolet stabilized shall not remain uncovered for longer than seven days. Ultraviolet stabilized material shall not remain exposed for longer than 30 days. Should the geotextile be torn or punctured or the overlaps or joints disturbed, as evidenced by visible geotextile damage, subgrade pumping, intrusion, or roadbed distortion, the backfill around the damaged or displaced area shall be removed and the damaged geotextile repaired or replaced by the Contractor at no cost to the Owner. The repair shall consist of a patch of the same type geotextile placed over the ruptured area. The patch shall overlap the existing fabric a minimum of 18 inches from the edge of the rupture.
